newsitem.title: USA: Tidewater says still on target for EPS rise.
newsitem.headline: Tidewater says still on target for EPS rise.

text.p: Tidewater Inc on Monday said it still expected its acquisition of Ocean Group Plc's O.I.L. Ltd subsidiary to add two cents a share to earnings despite a delay in British approval of the deal and the announcement of new builds on Friday.
Tidewater Chairman William O'Malley said he did not see any obstacles to British approval. He now expects the deal to close by May 16.
Citing an announcement on Friday that Edison Chouest would commission 17 new vessels, O'Malley said they would not have an impact on the offshore drilling capacity for 2 to 3 years.
Tidewater shares fell three points and the stock sunk as low as 35-7/8 on monday before clawing back some losses to trade down 4-3/4 at 39-3/4 by early afternoon
"We do not need to be concerned about this announcement for the next two to three years," O'Malley said. He said the new vessels were aimed at the deepwater market.
Chouest said Friday it had ordered 10 vessels with an option on an additional seven.
Laney Chouest, senior vice president at Edison Chouest, told the Tidewater conference call that he did not believe the new capacity would compete with Tidewater's.

"It is like saying that if the Chicago Bulls lost, then shares in the Atlanta Braves should be marked down," Chouest said, although Chouest added that he had firm contracts for all the proposed vessels.
O'Malley said that if U.S. dayrates for offshore service vessels started to weaken, then he would delay bringing back capacity from overseas.
He said additional pipeline and platform work as new fields were developed would remove some support capacity from the industry.
If dayrates do slide, Tidewater would also mothball some of its capacity.
The company is due to release its earnings on Thursday and O'Malley said, "I am sure you will not be disappointed."
